**Conversation Overview**

This conversation is a continuation of a long-running computational physics research project called the Löwdin project (session 18), which uses a handoff-pack protocol to preserve state across chat sessions. The person is directing Claude through a structured scientific computation involving atomic orbital eigenvalues, relativistic corrections, and exchange potentials for a series of elements (transition metals, lanthanides, and heavy elements). The session opened with Claude loading LOWDIN-HANDOFF-17 (a tar archive with 271 files), running four mandatory verification gates, and reviewing the session bridge document before any new work began.

The session completed three major computational tasks. First, T7b (exact Fock/Hartree-Fock exchange on a logarithmic mesh) was audited from abandoned-branch artefacts found in the container (fault F18.1), then adopted after passing three gates (He 1s eigenvalue −0.91796, Ne 2p −0.85041 matching Fischer 1977 standards; Dirac-switch regenerating T5 HFS-TS exactly; Janak identity verified). T7b results showed exact exchange removes approximately half the 4f shell-constant offset, has no leverage on 5d, and breaks Cu (+27%). Predictions PB1 and PB3 failed; PB2 held (TS/ΔSCF agreement ≤2%); PB4 could not fire. Second, a formal additive sum test (T7c + T7b) was run and retired: it overshoots all four 4f species on both spin-averaged and polarised objects. Third, SR re-probes of corridor residues (Ra II, Th IV, Lr I, Sr II, Ce IV, Pr V) were run in two phases — frozen kernel and self-consistent — with predictions stated before each run. Key outcomes: Ra II ordering corrected to +0.041 Ha (measured +0.055); Lr I spin-orbit gap quantified at +0.068 Ha scalar; Ce IV and Pr V show relativistic shares of 0.12–0.14 Ha toward measurement.

The person's working protocol is strict and well-established: predictions must be written before any run; faults are registered before results are read; nothing is written to the register/index/store without explicit ruling; the handoff archive is a single superset tar with a verify script; the session-state trigger for handoff is 90% context; and T4 writing chat is always last. The person gave terse directional rulings ("Go," "2 please," "continue") and corrected Claude once on the handoff trigger threshold, clarifying it is 90% per the project instructions' first item, not the 85% Claude had assumed. The session sealed LOWDIN-HANDOFF-18.tar.gz (sha `f534ccd16072673b`, 297 files, 297/297 verified), with the bridge naming candidate §3(1′) — self-consistent SR spin-polarised probe on Ce IV, Pr V, and Ra II — as the next smallest build requiring a ruling and pre-run prediction in the next session.

<chat url='https://claude.ai/chat/bfabd67e-32d5-4401-bf96-4f7933c681a2' updated_at='2026-08-16T20:47:10.365672+00:00'>Title: LCP15
Summary: **Conversation Overview**

This conversation is session 17 of an ongoing long-running computational physics project codenamed LOWDIN (CODE-LOWDIN-2_13). The session opened with Claude executing a multi-step handoff protocol: reviewing project knowledge, reading prior chat transcripts (identifying LCP14/session 16 as the latest), extracting and verifying the LOWDIN-HANDOFF-16 archive (SHA prefix f0fd43d3, 258/258 files verified), assembling a runtime environment, and passing three gates confirming code integrity before reading the session bridge, build specification, and recorded predictions.

The primary task of session 17 was executing T7c: building and running a scalar-relativistic radial kernel based on the Koelling–Harmon (1977) formulation to test whether relativistic effects account for the shell-constant 4f ionization energy offset identified in prior sessions. Claude built t7c_kernel.py implementing the KH equation via the substitution P = M^{1/2}F (eliminating the first-derivative term so the existing C Numerov shoot and bisection machinery could be reused unchanged), with M = 1 + (E−V)/2c², c = 137.035999 atomic units, no fitted constant. A fault in the C shoot kernel's starting exponent (F17.1) was caught by gate (ii) before any species result was read and repaired via shoot_sr.c using slope √q₀. A second precision limitation (F17.2) regarding rmin placement was accepted as a stated limit. Two gate checks passed: c→∞ reproduced the banked T5/T6 nonrelativistic values exactly; H 1s at physical c matched the Dirac energy to 3×10⁻⁷ Ha. The kernel was then run on all ten species (Dy, Er, Tm, Yb, Fe, La, Gd, Lu, Sc, Cu) in spin-averaged HFS-TS, spin-averaged ΔSCF, and spin-polarised TS modes, with snapshots after each batch.

Key findings: the SR kernel removes the shell-constant 4f offset entirely (shift/offset ratio 0.83–1.19 across the four lanthanides), with the spin-polarised object placing all four 4f species inside the ~15% measurement band (Dy +8.6%, Er −15.1%, Tm −9.8%, Yb 0.0%). The nonrelativistic Dy→Yb deepening trend disappears under SR. Cost: 5d orbitals (La, Gd, Lu) are relativistically destabilised (the known indirect effect), moving from ~2% to the band edge (12.9–15.1% shallow, growing La→Lu). 3d controls (Sc, Fe, Cu) are unaffected. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""hfs.py -- Session 8, T1': a DERIVABLE kernel improvement at f. No new constant.

WHAT CHANGES AND WHAT DOES NOT. tfd.py builds V = -Z/r + V_es[rho_TF] + V_x[rho_TF] with Dirac's local
exchange V_x = -(3 rho/pi)^(1/3) (that is the D in TFD) and the Latter tail V <= -q/r. Here the SAME three
pieces are kept and only the density is replaced: rho from the occupied one-electron orbitals of the same
potential, iterated to self-consistency. That is Gaspar 1954 / Kohn-Sham 1965 exchange-only, run as
Herman-Skillman 1963 did (with Latter's tail). Occupations are the OBSERVED ground configuration of the
Z-1 core electrons (ground.py, NIST 5.12) -- the same core the charge-1 TFD object represents statistically.
Nothing is chosen: same nucleus, same exchange functional, same tail, same core count; the density is now
the orbitals' own. Mixing fraction and convergence tolerance are numerics, not physics (result checked
invariant to them).

PREDICTIONS, stated before the run (R 1449):
  (P1) J_H(4f) at Tb moves DOWN toward the Tb3+ value 0.0351 but stays ABOVE it (an orbital-density
       one-electron F^k is HF-like, and HF-like F^k exceed empirical ones). Not below.
  (P2) The four d-shell class steps (Mn Fe Tc Ru) and 5d/6d (Os Hs) stay IN: their windows are wide.
  (P3) 5f (Cm, Bk): NO confident prediction. Margins are 0.009-0.015 Ha under TFD; a self-consistent
       density can move both J_H and the E_B gaps by that much. This is the test the derived law must
       pass; if it fails here it fails honestly, and the failure is the finding.
  (P4) E_B gaps of the class species change by O(10 mHa); the ten class windows are therefore RECOMPUTED
       from the new kernel -- the law is evaluated inside one kernel, never TFD gaps against SCF P.
"""
import sys, json, numpy as np, tfd, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import step2_run, eigen_fix
from eigen_fix import eigen
from derive_P import numerov_wf as _numerov_wf, slater_Fk, J_H
import ground as G

def numerov_wf(V, l, n, zeta, Z, npts=3000):
    """derive_P.numerov_wf with the forbidden-region tail cleaned: for deep states the inward branch
    seeded at rmax underflows to noise long before the matching point. Zero u beyond the last point where
    |u| >= 1e-9 max|u| after the peak, renormalise, recount nodes. Identical to derive_P for the class
    species (their tails were clean at E ~ -0.3..-0.8) -- checked below in __main__."""
    r, dr, u, E, nd = _numerov_wf(V, l, n, zeta, Z, npts)
    a = np.abs(u); m = int(np.argmax(a)); thr = 1e-9*a[m]
    tail = np.where(a[m:] < thr)[0]
    if len(tail): u = u.copy(); u[m+tail[0]:] = 0.0
    u /= np.sqrt(np.sum(u*u*dr))
    sg = np.sign(u); sg = sg[sg != 0]; nd = int(np.sum(sg[1:] != sg[:-1]))
    return r, dr, u, E, nd

L = "spdfg"

def scf(Z, charge=1, npts=4000, beta=0.3, tol=2e-5, maxit=60, verbose=False):
    N = Z - charge; q = charge
    occ = list(G.expand(N)) if N > 0 else []      # (n, l, k) of the core, observed configuration; N=0 bare nucleus
    x = np.linspace(np.log(1e-6/Z), np.log(300.0), npts); r = np.exp(x); h = x[1]-x[0]; dr = r*h
    Vtfd, _ = tfd.potential(Z, charge)
    Vg = Vtfd(r)                                   # start from the TFD potential on the grid
    Vfun = lambda rr: np.interp(np.log(np.asarray(rr, float)), x, Vg)
    hist = []
    for it in range(maxit):
        n_r = np.zeros(npts); Es = {}
        for n, l, k in occ:
            rr, drr, u, E, nd = numerov_wf(Vfun, l, n, 1.0, Z)
            if nd != n-l-1: raise RuntimeError(f"Z={Z} it={it} {n}{L[l]} nodes {nd} != {n-l-1} E={E}")
            ui = np.interp(r, rr, u, left=0.0, right=0.0)
            ui /= np.sqrt(np.sum(ui*ui*dr))
            n_r += k*ui*ui; Es[(n, l)] = E
        # Hartree potential of the radial density n_r (int n_r dr = N)
        cum = np.cumsum(n_r*dr) - 0.5*n_r*dr
        outer = np.cumsum((n_r/r*dr)[::-1])[::-1] - 0.5*n_r/r*dr
        VH = cum/r + outer
        rho = n_r/(4*np.pi*r*r)
        Vx = -(3.0*rho/np.pi)**(1.0/3.0)           # Dirac exchange, same as tfd.py's functional
        Vnew = np.minimum(-Z/r + VH + Vx, -q/r)     # Latter tail, same as tfd.py
        d = float(np.max(np.abs(r*(Vnew-Vg))[r < 60]))
        hist.append(d)
        Vg = (1-beta)*Vg + beta*Vnew
        Vfun = lambda rr, Vg=Vg: np.interp(np.log(np.asarray(rr, float)), x, Vg)
        if verbose: print(f"  it {it:2d}  max|r dV| = {d:.2e}", flush=True)
        if d < tol: break
    return Vfun, Es, hist, (r, dr, Vg)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # gate: cleaned numerov_wf reproduces derive_P's Tb 4f F^k in the TFD object exactly
    V,_ = tfd.potential(65,1); r,dr,u,E,nd = numerov_wf(V,3,4,1.0,65); F=slater_Fk(r,dr,u,(0,2,4,6))
    print("gate Tb 4f TFD: J_H", round(J_H(3,F),5), "(held 0.04018) nodes", nd)
    # sanity: neutral atoms (charge=0 not defined in tfd; use charge=1 objects and report core eigenvalues)
    for Z in (10, 18):
        Vf, Es, hist, _ = scf(Z, 1, verbose=False)
        print(f"Z={Z} charge 1: iters {len(hist)} final dV {hist[-1]:.1e}  core E:",
              {f"{n}{L[l]}": round(E, 4) for (n, l), E in Es.items()})

content.thinking:
I'm seeing the inward particular solution blow up to roughly -3e17 because integrating toward smaller m amplifies the growing homogeneous mode, picking up error from the imperfect adiabatic start that compounds exponentially. Then the B coefficient around 1e21 has to cancel this huge spurious term, which is a textbook catastrophic cancellation problem from integrating in the wrong direction for that solution branch.

The fix is to shrink the integration range (lower the cumulative growth threshold, say from 60 down to around 25) so the exponential amplification stays small enough that the admixture error doesn't swamp the actual particular solution.

Actually, a more robust fix is to build the particular solution via a Green's function using both homogeneous solutions, since that naturally stays bounded — but I need to be careful since each homogeneous solution still blows up exponentially past the matching point if integrated across the full mesh, so I should restrict each one to its own stable side.

I'm checking that the Green's function product stays bounded across the domain: y_out grows toward the matching point while y_in decays toward the outer boundary, so their product at x_<≤x_> remains small and well-behaved even near the origin where y_in can be large for higher l values.

But I'm worried about the integration accuracy—using trapezoid or Simpson's rule on the mesh loses the higher-order consistency that Numerov itself provides, so the eigenvalue convergence might only be O(h⁴) rather than better. With 4000 points on a log mesh, the trapezoid error could be around 2.5e-5 relative, which risks missing the five-decimal precision target, so I should look at how Fischer's MCHF approach handles this inhomogeneous equation instead.

Her trick is to start the inward particular solution from the previous iteration's orbital values at a point where the source term is negligible—since the old orbital nearly satisfies the equation already, this avoids the catastrophic cancellation that would occur if the inward particular solution grew much larger than the true solution before matching.…

Then I realize the key difference: in run(), the potential sum includes the b==a branch, which adds a within-shell exchange term for l=1 that I omitted in my standalone test — this term is attractive and proportional to P_a itself, which likely pulls ε down and could be responsible for inducing the spurious node.

My Yb total energy matches Fischer's closely, within a few mHa of mesh differences. Looking at the 4f ionization energy, HF-ΔSCF undershoots the measured value by about 25%, HFS-ΔSCF overshoots by 55%, and HF-Transition State gives an even larger deviation, suggesting TS is a poor approximation for localized 4f orbitals in HF.

Now I'm noticing an inconsistency: if ε(N)=−0.73 and the half-occupation ε is −1.05, the Slater integral formula for ΔSCF should give something close to −1, not the −0.41 I calculated — so either the bracketing found the wrong root for the half-occupied orbital energy, or there's an error in how I'm combining the total energies. I recall the measured Yb 4f binding energy of 0.327 Ha corresponds to the known ionization energy of about 8.9 eV for the 4f13 6s2 hole state, which matches what I used as the reference.

I realize the subtlety: in HF, ∂E/∂q_a isn't simply ε_a because of the self-interaction term — it's ε_a plus half the orbital's own Coulomb-exchange contribution. This matches Janak's theorem only loosely, since the pair-counting energy expression isn't linear in occupation the way density functionals are.

I realize the q(q−1)/2 formula assumes integer occupation across the shell's spin-orbitals, but with fractional occupation spread evenly, the pair sum works out differently — giving q² scaled by a factor depending on shell degeneracy rather than q(q−1). So the fractional Janak-consistent energy expression needs its own distinct form rather than just substituting fractional q into the integer formula.

For HF-TS, the derivative-consistent Janak expression with fractional spin-orbital occupations would actually change the ground-state energy formula for open shells, but the average-of-configuration q(q−1)/2 is the physically correct multiplet-averaged energy for observed open-shell configurations like Dy 4f10 or Er 4f12 — the fractional-uniform version is really Slater's approximation rather than the true multiplet average.

I'm realizing the two formulas diverge for open shells — the true multiplet-averaged ΔSCF uses q(q−1)/2 which correctly vanishes self-interaction for a single electron like La 5d1, while the fractional-uniform TS form gives a spurious nonzero self-interaction term in that case. This suggests I need to keep ΔSCF and TS as genuinely distinct formulas rather than trying to unify them into one smooth functional.

Plugging in numbers for Yb's 4f shell, I get ε_TS around −0.6 Ha using the half-occupancy formula, but that's still noticeably off from the ΔSCF value of −0.41 — the two should agree much more closely if the transition-state theorem is working correctly, so something in my derivation must still be inconsistent.

If it does, that confirms internal consistency between the ΔSCF and transition-state approaches, similar to how the −0.5073 vs −0.528 comparison worked out earlier. But first I should question my assumption that E is strictly quadratic in occupation number for this shell.…

    species (their tails were clean at E ~ -0.3..-0.8) -- checked below in __main__."""

    sg = np.sign(u); sg = sg[sg != 0]; nd = int(np.sum(sg[1:] != sg[:-1]))

"""t7b_hf.py -- T7b (session 18): exact (Fock 1930) exchange on the log mesh, same loop/grid/objects as t5_scf.scf_occ.
hf_occ(Z, occ, qtail, exch='fock'|'dirac'): exch='dirac' is the local-Dirac branch and must regenerate scf_occ (T5 gate);
exch='fock' is HF written as Slater's per-orbital exact-exchange local potential  V_x^i(r) = X_i(r)/P_i(r),
   X_i(r) = - sum_j q_j sum_k w_k(l_i,l_j) Y^k_ij(r) P_j(r) / r ,   w_k = 1/2 * (l_i k l_j; 0 0 0)^2 ,
spin-averaged fractional-occupation form (q_j = shell occupation, fractional allowed; j runs over all shells incl. i).
Exact HF at self-consistency where P_i != 0. Node neighbourhoods |P_i| < delta*max|P_i| are bridged by linear
interpolation of V_x^i in log r (numerical procedure, sensitivity tested at the Ne 2s gate); beyond the last good
point V_x^i continues as 1/r. Energy: E = sum q eps - E_H - E_x,  E_H = 1/2 int n V_H,  E_x = -1/2 sum_ij q_i q_j sum_k w_k R^k(ij).
Gate (Fischer 1977, MEASURED-STANDARD, not fitted): He 1s eps -0.91796 ; Ne 2p eps -0.85041.
"""
import numpy as np, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from math import factorial as fac
import tfd, ground as G
from hfs import numerov_wf, L

def tj2(l1, k, l2):
    """(l1 k l2; 0 0 0)^2"""
    J = l1 + k + l2
    if J % 2 or k < abs(l1 - l2) or k > l1 + l2: return 0.0
    g = J // 2
    a = fac(g) / (fac(g - l1) * fac(g - k) * fac(g - l2))
    return a * a * fac(2*g - 2*l1) * fac(2*g - 2*k) * fac(2*g - 2*l2) / fac(2*g + 1)

def yk_over_r(r, dr, Pi, Pj, k):
    w = Pi * Pj * dr
    A = np.cumsum(w * r**k) - 0.5 * w * r**k
    B = np.cumsum((w * r**(-(k+1)))[::-1])[::-1] - 0.5 * w * r**(-(k+1))
    return A / r**(k+1) + B * r**k

def hf_occ(Z, occ, qtail, exch='fock', npts=4000, beta=0.3, tol=2e-5, maxit=80, delta=0.03):
    N = sum(k for _, _, k in occ)
    x = np.linspace(np.log(1e-6/Z), np.log(300.0), npts); r = np.exp(x); h = x[1]-x[0]; dr = r*h
    Vt, _ = tfd.potential(Z, max(int(round(Z-N)), 1)); Vg0 = Vt(r)
    Vg = {(n, l): Vg0.copy() for n, l, k in occ}
    mk = lambda V: (lambda rr, V=V: np.interp(np.log(np.asarray(rr, float)), x, V))
    Vf = {key: mk(V) for key, V in Vg.items()}
    for it in range(maxit):
        n_r = np.zeros(npts); Es = {}; P = {}
        for n, l, k in occ:
            rr, drr, u, E, nd = numerov_wf(Vf[(n, l)], l, n, 1.0, Z)
            if nd != n-l-1: raise RuntimeError(f"Z={Z} {n}{L[l]} nodes {nd}")
            ui = np.interp(r, rr, u, left=0.0, right=0.0); ui /= np.sqrt(np.sum(ui*ui*dr))
            n_r += k*ui*ui; Es[(n, l)] = E; P[(n, l)] = ui
        cum = np.cumsum(n_r*dr) - 0.5*n_r*dr; outer = np.cumsum((n_r/r*dr)[::-1])[::-1] - 0.5*n_r/r*dr; VH = cum/r + outer
        Vx = {}; Ex = 0.0
        if exch == 'dirac':
            rho = n_r/(4*np.pi*r*r); vx = -(3.0*rho/np.pi)**(1.0/3.0)
            for key in P: Vx[key] = vx
            Ex = 0.25*np.sum(n_r*vx*dr)*2  # E_x(Dirac) = 1/2 int n Vx * (3/4)... kept as scf_occ: Etot uses -1/4 int n Vx
        else:
            for ni, li, qi in occ:
                Pi = P[(ni, li)]; X = np.zeros(npts)
                for nj, lj, qj in occ:
                    Pj = P[(nj, lj)]
                    for k in range(abs(li-lj), li+lj+1, 2):
                        w = 0.5*tj2(li, k, lj)
                        Y = yk_over_r(r, dr, Pi, Pj, k)
                        X -= qj*w*Y*Pj
                        Ex -= 0.5*qi*qj*w*np.sum(Pi*Pj*Y*dr)
                a = np.abs(Pi); good = a > delta*a.max()
                ig = np.where(good)[0]; v = np.empty(npts)
                v[ig] = X[ig]/Pi[ig]
                v = np.interp(x, x[ig], v[ig])                # bridges nodes; constant beyond ends
                last = ig[-1]; v[last+1:] = v[last]*r[last]/r[last+1:]   # 1/r continuation of the tail
                Vx[(ni, li)] = v
        d = 0.0; Vn = {}
        for key in P:
            V = -Z/r + VH + Vx[key]
            if exch == 'dirac': V = np.minimum(V, -qtail/r)
            Vn[key] = V; d = max(d, float(np.max(np.abs(r*(V-Vg[key]))[r < 60])))
        for key in P: Vg[key] = (1-beta)*Vg[key] + beta*Vn[key]
        Vf = {key: mk(V) for key, V in Vg.items()}
        if d < tol: break
    if exch == 'dirac':
        Etot = sum(k*Es[(n, l)] for n, l, k in occ) - 0.5*np.sum(n_r*VH*dr) - 0.25*np.sum(n_r*Vx[list(P)[0]]*dr)
    else:
        Etot = sum(k*Es[(n, l)] for n, l, k in occ) - 0.5*np.sum(n_r*VH*dr) - Ex
    return Vf, Es, Etot, it+1

def ground_occ(Z): return [tuple(t) for t in G.expand(Z)]
def minus(occ, n, l, k):
    o = [list(t) for t in occ]
    for t in o:
        if t[0] == n and t[1] == l: t[2] -= k
    return [tuple(t) for t in o if t[2] > 1e-9]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    delta = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0.03
    # GATE A: Fischer 1977 HF eigenvalues (measured-standard). He 1s -0.91796 ; Ne 2p -0.85041 (2s -1.93039, 1s -32.7724 also listed)
    Vf, Es, E, it = hf_occ(2, [(1, 0, 2)], 1, 'fock', delta=delta)
    print(f"He 1s hf {Es[(1,0)]:.5f}  std -0.91796  Etot {E:.5f} (HF -2.86168)  it {it}  delta {delta}")
    Vf, Es, E, it = hf_occ(10, [(1, 0, 2), (2, 0, 2), (2, 1, 6)], 1, 'fock', delta=delta)
    print(f"Ne 2p hf {Es[(2,1)]:.5f}  std -0.85041 | 2s {Es[(2,0)]:.5f} std -1.93039 | 1s {Es[(1,0)]:.4f} std -32.7724 | Etot {E:.4f} (HF -128.5471)  it {it}")

    a = fac(g) / (fac(g - l1) * fac(g - k) * fac(g - l2))
    return a * a * fac(2*g - 2*l1) * fac(2*g - 2*k) * fac(2*g - 2*l2) / fac(2*g + 1)

def yk_over_r(r, dr, Pi, Pj, k):
    w = Pi * Pj * dr
    A = np.cumsum(w * r**k) - 0.5 * w * r**k
    B = np.cumsum((w * r**(-(k+1)))[::-1])[::-1] - 0.5 * w * r**(-(k+1))
    return A / r**(k+1) + B * r**k

def hf_occ(Z, occ, qtail, exch='fock', npts=4000, beta=0.3, tol=2e-5, maxit=80, delta=0.03):
    N = sum(k for _, _, k in occ)
    x = np.linspace(np.log(1e-6/Z), np.log(300.0), npts); r = np.exp(x); h = x[1]-x[0]; dr = r*h
    Vt, _ = tfd.potential(Z, max(int(round(Z-N)), 1)); Vg0 = Vt(r)
    Vg = {(n, l): Vg0.copy() for n, l, k in occ}
    mk = lambda V: (lambda rr, V=V: np.interp(np.log(np.asarray(rr, float)), x, V))
    Vf = {key: mk(V) for key, V in Vg.items()}
    for it in range(maxit):
        n_r = np.zeros(npts); Es = {}; P = {}
        for n, l, k in occ:
            rr, drr, u, E, nd = numerov_wf(Vf[(n, l)], l, n, 1.0, Z)
            if nd != n-l-1: raise RuntimeError(f"Z={Z} {n}{L[l]} nodes {nd}")
            ui = np.interp(r, rr, u, left=0.0, right=0.0); ui /= np.sqrt(np.sum(ui*ui*dr))
            n_r += k*ui*ui; Es[(n, l)] = E; P[(n, l)] = ui
        cum = np.cumsum(n_r*dr) - 0.5*n_r*dr; outer = np.cumsum((n_r/r*dr)[::-1])[::-1] - 0.5*n_r/r*dr; VH = cum/r + outer
        Vx = {}; Ex = 0.0
        if exch == 'dirac':
            rho = n_r/(4*np.pi*r*r); vx = -(3.0*rho/np.pi)**(1.0/3.0)
            for key in P: Vx[key] = vx
            Ex = 0.25*np.sum(n_r*vx*dr)*2  # E_x(Dirac) = 1/2 int n Vx * (3/4)... kept as scf_occ: Etot uses -1/4 int n Vx
        else:
            for ni, li, qi in occ:
                Pi = P[(ni, li)]; X = np.zeros(npts)
                for nj, lj, qj in occ:
                    Pj = P[(nj, lj)]
                    for k in range(abs(li-lj), li+lj+1, 2):
                        w = 0.5*tj2(li, k, lj)
                        Y = yk_over_r(r, dr, Pi, Pj, k)
                        X -= qj*w*Y*Pj
                        Ex -= 0.5*qi*qj*w*np.sum(Pi*Pj*Y*dr)
                a = np.abs(Pi); good = a > delta*a.max()
                ig = np.where(good)[0]; v = np.empty(npts)
                v[ig] = X[ig]/Pi[ig]
                v = np.interp(x, x[ig], v[ig])                # bridges nodes; constant beyond ends
                last = ig[-1]; v[last+1:] = v[last]*r[last]/r[last+1:]   # 1/r continuation of the tail
                Vx[(ni, li)] = v
        d = 0.0; Vn = {}
        for key in P:
            V = -Z/r + VH + Vx[key]
            if exch == 'dirac': V = np.minimum(V, -qtail/r)
            Vn[key] = V; d = max(d, float(np.max(np.abs(r*(V-Vg[key]))[r < 60])))
        for key in P: Vg[key] = (1-beta)*Vg[key] + beta*Vn[key]
        Vf = {key: mk(V) for key, V in Vg.items()}
        if d < tol: break
    if exch == 'dirac':
        Etot = sum(k*Es[(n, l)] for n, l, k in occ) - 0.5*np.sum(n_r*VH*dr) - 0.25*np.sum(n_r*Vx[list(P)[0]]*dr)
    else:
        Etot = sum(k*Es[(n, l)] for n, l, k in occ) - 0.5*np.sum(n_r*VH*dr) - Ex
    return Vf, Es, Etot, it+1

def ground_occ(Z): return [tuple(t) for t in G.expand(Z)]

            out=shoot(e)
            if out is None or not np.isfinite(out[1]) or out[1]<=0: return None
            return math.log(out[1]),out
        hi=eh-1e-7*abs(eh); rhi=g(hi)
        if getattr(self,'dbg',False): print(f"   dbg {n}{L[l]} eh {eh:.6f} lnN(hi) {rhi[0] if rhi else None}",flush=True)
        if rhi is None or rhi[0]<0:            # source pushes the other way (rare): search upward
            lo,rlo=hi,rhi; step=0.02*abs(eh)+1e-4
            for _ in range(60):
                hi=lo+step; rhi=g(hi)
                if rhi is not None and rhi[0]>0: break
                lo,rlo=hi,rhi; step*=1.5
        else:
            step=0.02*abs(eh)+1e-4; lo=hi-step; rlo=g(lo)
            for _ in range(60):
                if rlo is not None and rlo[0]<0: break
                step*=1.6; lo=hi-step; rlo=g(lo)
        best=None
        for it in range(80):
            mid=0.5*(lo+hi); rm=g(mid)
            if getattr(self,'dbg',False) and rm is not None: print(f"   dbg {n}{L[l]} e {mid:.6f} lnN {rm[0]:+.3e} nd {rm[1][2]}",flush=True)
            if rm is None: hi=mid; continue
            if abs(rm[0])<1e-11 or hi-lo<1e-13*max(1,abs(mid)): best=(mid,rm[1]); break
            if rm[0]>0: hi=mid
            else: lo=mid
        if best is None: best=(mid,rm[1])
        e,(u,nrm,nd)=best
        u=u/np.sqrt(nrm)
        return u,e,nd,abs(math.log(nrm))
    def run(self, mode='hf', qtail=1, beta=0.4, tol=2e-6, maxit=100, seed=None, verbose=False):
        occ=self.occ; r,dr=self.r,self.dr
        P,eps=seed if seed is not None else self.seed(qtail)
        keys=[(n,l) for n,l,q in occ]; Q={(n,l):q for n,l,q in occ}
        hist=[]
        for it in range(maxit):
            n_r=sum(Q[k]*P[k]*P[k] for k in keys)
            if mode=='hfs':
                cum=np.cumsum(n_r*dr)-0.5*n_r*dr; outer=np.cumsum((n_r/r*dr)[::-1])[::-1]-0.5*n_r/r*dr; VH=cum/r+outer
                rho=n_r/(4*np.pi*r*r); Vx=-(3.0*rho/np.pi)**(1.0/3.0)
                Vall=np.minimum(-self.Z/r+VH+Vx,-qtail/r)
            Y0={k:self.Yk(P[k],P[k],0) for k in keys}
            newP={}; neweps={}; dmax=0.0
            for a in keys:
                n,l=a
                if mode=='hfs': Vloc=Vall; X=np.zeros(self.npts)
                else:
                    Vloc=-self.Z/r+sum((Q[b]-(1.0 if b==a else 0.0))*Y0[b]/r for b in keys)
                    X=np.zeros(self.npts)
                    for b in keys:
                        nb,lb=b
                        if b==a:                      # within-shell exchange is LOCAL (prop. to P_a): into Vloc
                            w=(2*l+1)/(4*l+1); c=(Q[a]-1.0)*w
                            if abs(c)>1e-14:
                                for k in range(2,2*l+1,2): Vloc=Vloc-c*_c3j0sq(l,k,l)*self.Yk(P[a],P[a],k)/r
                        else:
                            for k in range(abs(l-lb),l+lb+1,2): X+=0.5*Q[b]*_c3j0sq(l,k,lb)*self.Yk(P[a],P[b],k)/r*P[b]
                u,e,nd,res=self.solve_one(l,n,Vloc,X,eps[a],P[a])
                if nd!=n-l-1: raise RuntimeError(f"Z={self.Z} {n}{L[l]} nodes {nd}!={n-l-1} eps={e:.4f} mode={mode}")
                if np.sum(u*P[a]*dr)<0: u=-u
                dmax=max(dmax,abs(e-eps[a]))
                newP[a]=(1-beta)*P[a]+beta*u; newP[a]/=np.sqrt(np.sum(newP[a]**2*dr)); neweps[a]=(1-beta)*eps[a]+beta*e
            P,eps=newP,neweps; hist.append(dmax)
            if verbose: print(f"  it {it:3d} max|d eps| {dmax:.2e}",flush=True)
            if dmax<tol and it>2: break
        # total energy at convergence (unmixed final quantities from a last evaluation)
        self.P,self.eps=P,eps
        Etot=self.energy(mode,qtail)
        return eps,Etot,it+1,hist

        P,eps,Q=self.P,self.eps,{(n,l):q for n,l,q in self.occ}; r,dr=self.r,self.dr; keys=list(P)
        if mode=='hfs':
            n_r=sum(Q[k]*P[k]*P[k] for k in keys)
            cum=np.cumsum(n_r*dr)-0.5*n_r*dr; outer=np.cumsum((n_r/r*dr)[::-1])[::-1]-0.5*n_r/r*dr; VH=cum/r+outer
            rho=n_r/(4*np.pi*r*r); Vx=-(3.0*rho/np.pi)**(1.0/3.0)
            return sum(Q[k]*eps[k] for k in keys)-0.5*np.sum(n_r*VH*dr)-0.25*np.sum(n_r*Vx*dr)

                nb,lb=b
                if b==a:
                    w=(2*l+1)/(4*l+1); c=(Q[a]-1.0)*w
                    for k in range(2,2*l+1,2): Vloc=Vloc-c*_c3j0sq(l,k,l)*self.Yk(P[a],P[a],k)/r
                else:
                    for k in range(abs(l-lb),l+lb+1,2): X+=0.5*Q[b]*_c3j0sq(l,k,lb)*self.Yk(P[a],P[b],k)/r*P[b]
            Ia=eps[a]-np.sum(P[a]*(Vloc+self.Z/r)*P[a]*dr)+np.sum(P[a]*X*dr)   # I = <T - Z/r>
            E+=0.5*Q[a]*(eps[a]+Ia)
        return float(E)

I'm noticing the foreign run uses a modified Hartree-Fock expression adding a half-J̃ correction to the orbital energy, since the plain average-of-configuration epsilon at half occupation isn't truly Janak-consistent—the self-Coulomb removal means the derivative of energy with respect to occupation doesn't match epsilon in Fischer's formulation. They claim this correction was verified exactly against the energy difference via Simpson's method on ytterbium.

Working through the derivative myself, the within-shell energy term scales with q(q-1)/2 times J̃, so its derivative with respect to occupation gives (q-½)J̃, while epsilon itself (built from the (q-1) operator) only contributes (q-1)J̃ — meaning the true Janak derivative is epsilon plus half J̃,…

Gate: c=1e6 regenerates the nonrel probe to 1e-4. Predictions PS1-PS4 stated in chat before this file ran. Appends t7c_scres.jsonl."""
import sys, json, os, io, contextlib, time, numpy as np, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import eigen_fix
from t5_scf import scf_occ, ground_occ
from t7c_kernel import scf_occ_sr, eigen_sr

    Z,N,pairs,meas=IONS[lab]; q=Z-N; g=ground_occ(N); t0=time.time()
    if mode=='nr':
        Vf,Es,E,it=scf_occ(Z,g,q); e=[eigen_fix.eigen(Vf,l,n,2.0,Z) for n,l in pairs]
    elif mode=='gate':
